title: Hom complex from a K-flat into a K-injective complex is K-injective
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal L^\bullet$ be a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex] and $\mathcal I^\bullet$ a K-injective complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then the Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is K-injective.

proof.text: For an arbitrary acyclic test complex K and chain map f : K → Hom(L,I), let T = Tot(K ⊗ L). Apply the recorded definition of K-flatness to obtain T.Acyclic.

Obtain the isomorphism t : Hom(K,Hom(L,I)) ≅ Hom(T,I) from homComplex_tensorTotal_iso. Apply the global-cochain comparison to both sides. Represent the degree-zero cochain of f by a morphism z from the rank-one module sheaf to the degree-zero term of Hom(K,Hom(L,I)). Differential compatibility and δ(ofHom f)=0 imply z d = 0. The chain-map equation for t shows that b_0(z t_0) is an external cocycle from T to I.

Use Mathlib CochainComplex.IsKInjective.eq_δ_of_cocycle with the acyclic T to express this cocycle as δα for a degree-minus-one cochain α. Represent α by b_{-1}^{-1}(α), then postcompose with t^{-1}_{-1}. The inverse-isomorphism and chain-map identities show that its differential is z. Differential compatibility of a gives δ(a_{-1}(s)) = ofHom f. Mathlib Cochain.equivHomotopy converts this equality into Homotopy f 0. Supply these homotopies to the IsKInjective constructor.
